1	// Package review — see env.go for package-level rationale.
2	//
3	// synthesis_sink.go provides SynthesisSink, the master adjudication phase of a
4	// multi-agent review: after all worker agents finish, it asks a configured
5	// provider to consolidate the per-agent narratives into a final report.
6	// Skipped silently on cancellation or when fewer than 2 successful agents
7	// produced usable output. The report runs unconditionally (no y/N prompt) and works in
8	// both TTY and redirected/CI output.
9	//
10	// Composition: appended AFTER DumpSink in the multi-agent sink slice, so the
11	// final report renders below the per-agent narrative dump.
12	package review
13	
14	import (
15		"context"
16		"fmt"
17		"io"
18		"time"
19	
20		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent"
21		agenttypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types"
22		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/mdrender"
23		reviewtypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/review/types"
24	)
25	
26	// SynthesisProvider abstracts the LLM call that produces the cross-agent
27	// verdict. Injected so tests can stub the provider call without a real API
28	// roundtrip; production wiring uses AgentSynthesisProvider.
29	type SynthesisProvider interface {
30		// Synthesize takes the composed synthesis prompt and returns the
31		// verdict text. On error the sink prints "final report unavailable" and
32		// signals OnError; the command then surfaces an attempted-but-failed
33		// synthesis as a non-zero exit (see runMultiAgentPath).
34		Synthesize(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (string, error)
35	}
36	
37	// AgentSynthesisProvider asks a named agent's text-generation API to produce
38	// the final report. This is the profile-native master implementation used by
39	// `entire review`: workers run as review sessions, while the master is an
40	// isolated text-generation call so it consolidates reports without creating a
41	// second review worker session.
42	type AgentSynthesisProvider struct {
43		AgentName string
44		Model     string
45	}
46	
47	func (p AgentSynthesisProvider) Synthesize(ctx context.Context, prompt string) (string, error) {
48		ag, err := agent.Get(agenttypes.AgentName(p.AgentName))
49		if err != nil {
50			return "", fmt.Errorf("resolve master agent %s: %w", p.AgentName, err)
51		}
52		tg, ok := agent.AsTextGenerator(ag)
53		if !ok {
54			return "", fmt.Errorf("master agent %s does not support text generation", p.AgentName)
55		}
56		return tg.GenerateText(ctx, prompt, p.Model) //nolint:wrapcheck // caller owns display
57	}
58	
59	// SynthesisSink composes a multi-agent verdict by calling a configured
60	// provider after the run finishes — the profile's master adjudication phase.
61	// Provider is the profile master, so the final report is produced
62	// unconditionally (no y/N prompt). AgentEvent is a no-op; all work happens in
63	// RunFinished.
64	type SynthesisSink struct {
65		Provider SynthesisProvider
66		Writer   io.Writer
67		// RenderWriter is the writer whose terminal capabilities should be used for
68		// markdown rendering. It defaults to Writer. TTY review runs use this when
69		// Writer is a post-run buffer that will later flush to the real terminal.
70		RenderWriter    io.Writer
71		PerRunPrompt    string // if non-empty, included in the synthesis prompt for context
72		ProfileName     string
73		Task            string
74		MasterName      string
75		RunContext      context.Context // optional; nil falls back to context.Background()
76		ProviderTimeout time.Duration   // positive: use it; zero: defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout; negative: disabled (no deadline)
77		OnResult        func(result string)
78		OnStart         func()
79		OnComplete      func(error)
80		// OnError is called when an attempted synthesis fails (provider error or
81		// timeout). It is NOT called when synthesis is skipped (cancelled run or
82		// fewer than two usable reviewers). Lets the caller surface a missing verdict
83		// in the command's exit status instead of exiting 0 with no final report.
84		OnError func(error)
85	}
86	
87	// Compile-time interface check.
88	var _ reviewtypes.Sink = SynthesisSink{}
89	
90	// defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout bounds the judge's single consolidation call
91	// when SynthesisSink.ProviderTimeout is unset. The judge reads every reviewer's
92	// report and writes the combined verdict in one text-generation call, which
93	// regularly needs more than the original 2m. 20m matches the judge's previous
94	// effective bound: before the reviewer default was dropped, the --timeout flag
95	// default (20m) always flowed into ProviderTimeout on the no-flag path, so
96	// keeping 5m here would have silently tightened the judge 4x — and a judge
97	// timeout discards an entire multi-reviewer run with no verdict.
98	const defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout = 20 * time.Minute
99	
100	// AgentEvent is a no-op; SynthesisSink only acts in RunFinished.
101	func (SynthesisSink) AgentEvent(_ string, _ reviewtypes.Event) {}
102	
103	// RunFinished synthesizes a cross-agent final report.
104	//
105	// Skip silently when:
106	//   - the run was cancelled (summary.Cancelled)
107	//   - fewer than 2 successful agents produced usable output
108	//
109	// The master phase is mandatory and runs without a y/N prompt, in TTY and
110	// redirected output alike. On provider failure: print "final report
111	// unavailable: <err>" with the underlying error; the user can still commit.
112	func (s SynthesisSink) RunFinished(summary reviewtypes.RunSummary) {
113		if summary.Cancelled {
114			return
115		}
116		if usableAgentCount(summary) < 2 {
117			return
118		}
119	
120		synthesisPrompt := composeSynthesisPrompt(summary, s.PerRunPrompt, s.ProfileName, s.Task)
121		providerCtx, cancelProvider := s.providerContext()
122		defer cancelProvider()
123		if s.MasterName != "" {
124			fmt.Fprintf(s.Writer, "Generating final report with %s...\n", s.MasterName)
125		} else {
126			fmt.Fprintln(s.Writer, "Generating final report...")
127		}
128		if s.OnStart != nil {
129			s.OnStart()
130		}
131		result, provErr := s.Provider.Synthesize(providerCtx, synthesisPrompt)
132		if provErr != nil {
133			fmt.Fprintf(s.Writer, "final report unavailable: %v\n", provErr)
134			if s.OnError != nil {
135				s.OnError(provErr)
136			}
137			if s.OnComplete != nil {
138				s.OnComplete(provErr)
139			}
140			return
141		}
142		if s.OnResult != nil {
143			s.OnResult(result)
144		}
145		// The synthesis verdict is markdown — render it through the same palette
146		// dispatch / DumpSink use, so multi-agent reviews finish with a visually
147		// consistent block. Non-TTY writers receive raw markdown unchanged.
148		//
149		// Use Fprint (not Fprintln): mdrender.Render returns glamour output that
150		// already ends with a newline, and the raw-markdown fallback path has its
151		// own terminal newline from the LLM response. Adding Fprintln would double
152		// the trailing blank line.
153		rendered, err := mdrender.RenderForWriter(s.renderWriter(), result)
154		if err != nil {
155			rendered = result
156		}
157		fmt.Fprint(s.Writer, rendered)
158		if s.OnComplete != nil {
159			s.OnComplete(nil)
160		}
161	}
162	
163	func (s SynthesisSink) renderWriter() io.Writer {
164		if s.RenderWriter != nil {
165			return s.RenderWriter
166		}
167		return s.Writer
168	}
169	
170	func (s SynthesisSink) runContext() context.Context {
171		if s.RunContext != nil {
172			return s.RunContext
173		}
174		return context.Background()
175	}

178	// the same three-state convention as the reviewer timeout so a single --timeout
179	// value can govern the whole command:
180	//   - positive: use it.
181	//   - zero (unset): use defaultSynthesisProviderTimeout.
182	//   - negative: disabled — no deadline (mirrors `--timeout 0` for reviewers).
183	func (s SynthesisSink) providerContext() (context.Context, context.CancelFunc) {
184		switch {
185		case s.ProviderTimeout < 0:
186			return context.WithCancel(s.runContext())
187		case s.ProviderTimeout > 0:

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

Root cause is confirmed. Let me now write up the diagnosis and the concrete fix plan for your approval before I change code across packages.

## Root cause

`entire review`'s judge is a one-shot CLI call through `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/text_generator_cli.go`). It spawns the judge binary (codex) with `exec.CommandContext`, captures stdout/stderr into `bytes.Buffer`s, and calls `cmd.Run()`. Its **only** bound is the 20-minute context deadline.

Two safeguards are missing:
1. **No `cmd.WaitDelay`** — after the deadline, `Run()`/`Wait()` blocks forever on the internal stdout/stderr copy goroutines.
2. **No process-group kill** — `exec.CommandContext`'s default cancel SIGKILLs only the direct child (codex). Codex's grandchildren (sandbox/node/MCP helpers) survive and keep the output pipe's write end open, so the copy goroutines never see EOF.

Net effect: at 20 min the deadline fires and kills codex, but the review process wedges in `cmd.Wait()` indefinitely. The spinner keeps ticking ("24m13s") because `Synthesize` never returns. This matches every observation: blocked, ~0% CPU, no codex child, no network, past the deadline.

The repo **already fixed this identical bug** for git subprocesses in `checkpoint/remote/command_cancel.go` (`terminateOnCancel`: `WaitDelay = 10s` + `killProcessGroupOnCancel`). The agent text-generator path just never got it. It affects every CLI-based judge/summary provider (codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, pi).

## Why

`entire review` can hang indefinitely at "Final judge is consolidating…", well past its 20-minute judge deadline. Observed live: the process sat blocked at ~0% CPU with no child processes and no network, the deadline having fired ~4 minutes earlier.

## Root cause

The judge runs through `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI`, which spawns the provider CLI with `exec.CommandContext` and captures stdout/stderr into `bytes.Buffer`s (so `os/exec` uses internal copy goroutines over OS pipes). Its only bound is the context deadline.

When the deadline fires, `exec.CommandContext`'s default cancel SIGKILLs **only the direct child**. The child's grandchildren — a sandbox/MCP helper the provider spawned — inherit the output pipe's write end and stay alive, so the copy goroutines never see EOF and `cmd.Run()` blocks forever. The deadline is silently defeated.

This affects every CLI-based judge/summary provider: codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, pi.

The repo already solved this exact "grandchild holds the pipe open, defeats ctx-cancel" problem for git subprocesses in `checkpoint/remote/command_cancel.go`. The agent text-generator path never got the same treatment.

## What changed

- New `execx.TerminateOnCancel`: sets `cmd.WaitDelay` (force-close pipes as a backstop) and a process-group SIGKILL on cancel (unix; no-op on Windows, WaitDelay still bounds it).
- Applied in `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI`, bounding all CLI-based providers.
- De-duplicated: `checkpoint/remote` now delegates to `execx`; its two platform files were deleted and the generic behavior tests moved to `execx`. The git subprocess path keeps identical behavior.
